title: Increment one shared counter under a lock from four threads
summary: Four threads each lock one shared mutex, take the next ticket from a counter and unlock, 2,000 to 50,000 times each, and the operation returns the final counter and the sum of all tickets.
notes: A task on four threads, all contending for one lock with a critical section of a read and a write. CPU time is the sum over all threads, so a lock that spins while it waits pays for the spinning, and one that parks pays in system calls and wakeups; wall-clock time is not what is ranked. Each operation creates the lock, starts its four threads and joins them; starting them is part of the figure. Go runs with GOMAXPROCS=4. CPython and CRuby run one thread at a time under their interpreter lock, so there the threads take turns and the lock is rarely contended. Expect high variance between rounds. No JavaScript entry: these are locks between threads.
